plan.planning_summary: Refining route_03 (28-layer non-periodic globally optimized stack) based on feedback to shift from purely randomized initialization to locally-biased bilayer-unit scheme. Four complementary routes proposed: (1) direct implementation of feedback with 28 layers in 14 bilayer units, quarter-wave initialized with ±15% tolerance and thickness-jump penalty; (2) reduced 20-layer variant to test performance vs. layer count tradeoff; (3) 28-layer with reversed material sequence (SiO2-first instead of HfO2-first) to test sequence sensitivity; (4) 26-layer chirped bilayer design with systematically varying optical thickness to explore graded-index-like behavior. All routes preserve the dual-band objective (high-T 1000-1700nm, high-R 300-450nm), fused silica substrate, HfO2/SiO2 materials, and ≤30 layer constraint.

routes.title: 28-Layer Bilayer-Unit Initialized Stack with Thickness-Jump Penalty
routes.scientific_hypothesis: Partitioning 28 layers into 14 contiguous HfO2/SiO2 bilayer units and initializing each unit around nominal quarter-wave optical thicknesses (±15% tolerance) with a soft penalty on inter-layer thickness jumps >40% will increase the fraction of physically valid candidates and improve best_target_score compared to purely randomized initialization, while preserving global non-periodicity across the stack.
routes.design_principle: Locally-biased initialization around quarter-wave estimates reduces search space volume while maintaining flexibility for non-quarter-wave optimization. Thickness-jump penalty prevents unrealistic layer thickness variations that cause numerical convergence failures.
routes.proposed_topology: Air | (HfO2 | SiO2) × 14 bilayer units | Fused Silica substrate. Total finite coating layers: 28. First layer (adjacent to air) is HfO2, last layer (adjacent to substrate) is SiO2.
design_variables: 28 individual layer thicknesses (nm), initialized per bilayer unit around quarter-wave at geometric mean wavelength of each band
soft_objectives: Maximize mean transmittance in 1000-1700 nm band
Maximize mean reflectance in 300-450 nm band
Minimize thickness variation between adjacent layers
manufacturing_considerations: Thickness-jump penalty reflects realistic deposition rate continuity
theory_basis: Quarter-wave stack theory: reflectivity maximizes for minimum layer count when optical thickness equals λ/4
Global optimization with bounded thickness: layer thickness bounded around reference wavelength estimates
expected_advantages: Higher valid_candidates count due to physically reasonable initialization
Improved best_target_score from better search space coverage
Reduced numerical_convergence failures compared to route_03
known_risks: May converge to local optimum near quarter-wave design rather than globally optimal non-quarter-wave solution
Thickness-jump penalty may overly constrain optimizer if penalty weight is too high
routes.execution_request_english: Optimize a 28-layer dielectric coating on fused silica substrate using HfO2 and SiO2 materials. Structure: Air incident | 14 contiguous bilayer units of (HfO2 | SiO2) | Fused Silica. Initialize each bilayer unit with HfO2 thickness = quarter-wave at 1350 nm (geometric mean of 1000-1700 nm band) and SiO2 thickness = quarter-wave at 375 nm (geometric mean of 300-450 nm band), with ±15% random tolerance per layer. Apply soft penalty during optimization to discourage thickness ratio between adjacent layers exceeding 1.4 or falling below 0.714. Optimize all 28 layer thicknesses independently. Evaluate at normal incidence, unpolarized light. Spectral bands: 300-450 nm (maximize reflectance), 1000-1700 nm (maximize transmittance). Use gradient-based thickness optimizer with 500 iterations maximum. Canonical user controls: wavelength intervals 300-450 nm, 1000-1700 nm. soft objectives: high transmission in 1000-1700 nm; high reflection in 300-450 nm. behaviors to suppress or avoid: low transmission in 300-450 nm; low reflection in 1000-1700 nm. manufacturing constraints: total layer count <= 30; materials restricted to HfO2 and SiO2.
routes.revision_reason: Directly implements feedback directive: shift from purely randomized initialization to locally-biased bilayer-unit scheme with quarter-wave estimates and thickness-jump penalty to address numerical_convergence failures observed in route_03.

routes.title: 20-Layer Reduced Count Bilayer-Unit Stack
routes.scientific_hypothesis: Reducing layer count from 28 to 20 (10 bilayer units) while maintaining bilayer-unit initialization will achieve comparable best_target_score with improved simplicity_score and reduced manufacturing complexity, testing whether route_03's 28 layers exceeded the minimum required for dual-band performance.
routes.design_principle: Fewer layers reduce cumulative thickness error, stress, and deposition time. If 20 layers achieve similar spectral performance, the design is more manufacturable and robust.
routes.proposed_topology: Air | (HfO2 | SiO2) × 10 bilayer units | Fused Silica substrate. Total finite coating layers: 20. First layer (adjacent to air) is HfO2, last layer (adjacent to substrate) is SiO2.
design_variables: 20 individual layer thicknesses (nm), initialized per bilayer unit around quarter-wave estimates with ±15% tolerance
soft_objectives: Maximize mean transmittance in 1000-1700 nm band
Maximize mean reflectance in 300-450 nm band
Maximize simplicity_score via reduced layer count
manufacturing_considerations: Total layer count 20 provides margin below 30 limit
Reduced layers decrease cumulative deposition error
theory_basis: Quarter-wave stack theory: reflectivity scales with layer pair count; diminishing returns beyond certain pair count
Global optimization with bounded thickness applied to reduced variable count
expected_advantages: Higher simplicity_score due to fewer layers
Potentially comparable best_target_score if 28 layers were over-designed
Faster optimization convergence due to fewer variables
known_risks: May not achieve sufficient reflectance in 300-450 nm band with fewer high-index/low-index pairs
Best_target_score may decrease relative to 28-layer designs
routes.execution_request_english: Optimize a 20-layer dielectric coating on fused silica substrate using HfO2 and SiO2 materials. Structure: Air incident | 10 contiguous bilayer units of (HfO2 | SiO2) | Fused Silica. Initialize each bilayer unit with HfO2 thickness = quarter-wave at 1350 nm and SiO2 thickness = quarter-wave at 375 nm, with ±15% random tolerance per layer. Apply soft penalty during optimization to discourage thickness ratio between adjacent layers exceeding 1.4 or falling below 0.714. Optimize all 20 layer thicknesses independently. Evaluate at normal incidence, unpolarized light. Spectral bands: 300-450 nm (maximize reflectance), 1000-1700 nm (maximize transmittance). Use differential evolution thickness optimizer with 300 iterations maximum. Canonical user controls: wavelength intervals 300-450 nm, 1000-1700 nm. soft objectives: high transmission in 1000-1700 nm; high reflection in 300-450 nm. behaviors to suppress or avoid: low transmission in 300-450 nm; low reflection in 1000-1700 nm. manufacturing constraints: total layer count <= 30; materials restricted to HfO2 and SiO2.
routes.revision_reason: Tests whether 28 layers in route_03 exceeded minimum required for dual-band performance. Reduced layer count may improve manufacturability and simplicity while maintaining acceptable performance.

routes.title: 28-Layer Reversed Sequence Bilayer-Unit Stack (SiO2-First)
routes.scientific_hypothesis: Reversing the bilayer sequence to start with SiO2 (low-index) at the air interface instead of HfO2 (high-index) will improve transmittance in 1000-1700 nm band due to better impedance matching at the air-coating interface, while maintaining comparable reflectance in 300-450 nm band.
routes.design_principle: Low-index first layer reduces Fresnel reflection at air-coating interface. For broadband AR applications, starting with lower index material improves initial impedance match.
routes.proposed_topology: Air | (SiO2 | HfO2) × 14 bilayer units | Fused Silica substrate. Total finite coating layers: 28. First layer (adjacent to air) is SiO2, last layer (adjacent to substrate) is HfO2.
design_variables: 28 individual layer thicknesses (nm), initialized per bilayer unit around quarter-wave estimates with ±15% tolerance
soft_objectives: Maximize mean transmittance in 1000-1700 nm band
Maximize mean reflectance in 300-450 nm band
Minimize front-surface reflection at air-coating interface
manufacturing_considerations: SiO2 outermost layer improves environmental durability per evidence
Reversed sequence may affect stress profile
theory_basis: Single-layer AR theory: perfect cancellation at normal incidence occurs when layer refractive index equals sqrt(n_substrate)
Graded index principle: starting with lower index creates smoother index transition
expected_advantages: Improved transmittance in 1000-1700 nm band due to better air-interface matching
SiO2 outermost layer provides environmental durability
May reduce sensitivity to angle of incidence
known_risks: May reduce reflectance in 300-450 nm band since high-index layer is not at air interface
Quarter-wave theory suggests high-index top layer maximizes reflectivity for HR stacks
routes.execution_request_english: Optimize a 28-layer dielectric coating on fused silica substrate using HfO2 and SiO2 materials. Structure: Air incident | 14 contiguous bilayer units of (SiO2 | HfO2) | Fused Silica. Initialize each bilayer unit with SiO2 thickness = quarter-wave at 1350 nm and HfO2 thickness = quarter-wave at 375 nm, with ±15% random tolerance per layer. Apply soft penalty during optimization to discourage thickness ratio between adjacent layers exceeding 1.4 or falling below 0.714. Optimize all 28 layer thicknesses independently. Evaluate at normal incidence, unpolarized light. Spectral bands: 300-450 nm (maximize reflectance), 1000-1700 nm (maximize transmittance). Use gradient-based thickness optimizer with 500 iterations maximum. Canonical user controls: wavelength intervals 300-450 nm, 1000-1700 nm. soft objectives: high transmission in 1000-1700 nm; high reflection in 300-450 nm. behaviors to suppress or avoid: low transmission in 300-450 nm; low reflection in 1000-1700 nm. manufacturing constraints: total layer count <= 30; materials restricted to HfO2 and SiO2.
routes.revision_reason: Tests material sequence sensitivity. Route_03 and route_03_ref_01 use HfO2-first; this route tests whether SiO2-first improves transmission band performance via better impedance matching at air interface.

routes.title: 26-Layer Chirped Bilayer-Unit Stack with Graded Optical Thickness
routes.scientific_hypothesis: A 26-layer chirped design (13 bilayer units) with systematically varying optical thickness across the stack will achieve broader spectral coverage in both bands compared to uniform quarter-wave initialization, trading peak performance for bandwidth robustness.
routes.design_principle: Chirped stacks vary layer optical thickness progressively to broaden reflection/transmission bands. Starting layers optimized for one band edge, ending layers for opposite band edge.
routes.proposed_topology: Air | 13 bilayer units of (HfO2 | SiO2) with chirped optical thickness | Fused Silica substrate. Total finite coating layers: 26. First layer is HfO2, last layer is SiO2. Bilayer optical thickness varies from 300 nm (band 1 center) to 1350 nm (band 2 center) across stack depth.
design_variables: 26 individual layer thicknesses (nm), initialized with linear chirp in optical thickness from front to back of stack
soft_objectives: Maximize mean transmittance in 1000-1700 nm band
Maximize mean reflectance in 300-450 nm band
Maximize bandwidth uniformity within each band
manufacturing_considerations: Chirped design requires precise thickness control per layer
May be more sensitive to deposition rate errors
theory_basis: Quarter-wave stack theory with non-uniform optical thickness for broadband applications
Graded index principle: varying layer thickness creates effective index gradient
expected_advantages: Broader spectral coverage in both bands
More uniform performance across band edges
Potentially better tolerance to wavelength drift
known_risks: May sacrifice peak performance in band centers
Chirp parameters require careful tuning; poor chirp may degrade both bands
routes.execution_request_english: Optimize a 26-layer dielectric coating on fused silica substrate using HfO2 and SiO2 materials. Structure: Air incident | 13 bilayer units of (HfO2 | SiO2) with chirped optical thickness | Fused Silica. Initialize bilayer optical thickness with linear chirp: front bilayers centered at 375 nm (300-450 nm band center), back bilayers centered at 1350 nm (1000-1700 nm band center), with intermediate bilayers linearly interpolated. Apply ±15% random tolerance per layer. Apply soft penalty during optimization to discourage thickness ratio between adjacent layers exceeding 1.4 or falling below 0.714. Optimize all 26 layer thicknesses independently. Evaluate at normal incidence, unpolarized light. Spectral bands: 300-450 nm (maximize reflectance), 1000-1700 nm (maximize transmittance). Use differential evolution thickness optimizer with 400 iterations maximum. Canonical user controls: wavelength intervals 300-450 nm, 1000-1700 nm. soft objectives: high transmission in 1000-1700 nm; high reflection in 300-450 nm. behaviors to suppress or avoid: low transmission in 300-450 nm; low reflection in 1000-1700 nm. manufacturing constraints: total layer count <= 30; materials restricted to HfO2 and SiO2.
routes.revision_reason: Explores chirped design as alternative to uniform quarter-wave initialization. Tests whether graded optical thickness improves bandwidth coverage for dual-band dichroic application, complementing the uniform initialization routes.

Whether chirped or uniform initialization provides better bandwidth coverage is unknown; route_03_ref_04 tests chirped approach
plan.stop_if_all_routes_fail: Stop after the bounded route portfolio is exhausted or further search stagnates. Return every physically verified candidate and report soft objective trade-offs without a performance admission threshold.
